components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and seasons, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn, 稻 rice.
子 (child) — 季 was the youngest child, then the last month of a season, then the season itself.

example.pinyin: Chūnjì shì zuì hǎo de jìjié.
example.english: Spring is the best season.
example.fact: 季 is mostly seen in 季节 (season), 四季 (the four seasons) and 季度 (quarter of a year), and compounds like 旺季 (peak season). It is also a surname.

examples.pinyin: Xiàjì de báitiān hěn cháng.
examples.english: The days are long in summer.

examples.pinyin: Zhège jìjié chángcháng xiàyǔ.
examples.english: It often rains in this season.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at seven every morning.
example.fact: Chinese splits "morning" three ways where English has one word: 早上 (colloquial, roughly dawn to mid-morning), 早晨 (close to 早上 but slightly more literary), and 上午 ("forenoon," extending all the way to noon and used in more neutral or formal contexts) — worth knowing which one native speakers actually reach for at a given hour.

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang hǎo, jīntiān zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: Good morning, how are you today?

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang pǎobù.
examples.english: He goes running every morning.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 别开这种玩笑,一点都不好笑。
example.pinyin: Bié kāi zhè zhǒng wánxiào, yìdiǎn dōu bù hǎoxiào.
example.english: Don't make this kind of joke, it's not funny at all.
example.fact: 玩笑 rarely stands as the object of a generic verb like "to make" — it almost always locks into the fixed collocation 开玩笑 ("to crack a joke," literally "to open a joke"), the same way English speakers reach for "crack" specifically before "a joke" rather than a general-purpose verb.

examples.pinyin: Tā ài kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: He loves to joke.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zài kāi wánxiào, bié shēngqì.
examples.english: I'm just joking, don't be angry.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 老师给我们布置了一项新任务。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen bùzhì le yí xiàng xīn rènwu.
example.english: The teacher assigned us a new task.
example.fact: 任务 carries a note of formal assignment — a task or mission handed down by someone in authority or an organization (军事任务 "military mission," 学习任务 "study assignment") — distinguishing it from the more neutral, everyday 事情 ("matter, thing to do") used for whatever's simply on one's plate.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de dì yī ge rènwu.
examples.english: This is my first assignment.

examples.pinyin: Tā wánchéngle suǒyǒu rènwu.
examples.english: He completed all the tasks.

meanings: the scene (of a crime, accident etc)

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 事故现场已经被警察封锁了。
example.pinyin: Shìgù xiànchǎng yǐjīng bèi jǐngchá fēngsuǒ le.
example.english: The accident scene has already been sealed off by the police.
example.fact: 现场 combines 现 ("present, now" — the same root behind 现在 in the companion pilot batch) with 场 ("a site, venue"), literally "the present site" — a word that carries both a spatial sense (the physical scene of an event) and a temporal-immediacy sense, as in 现场直播 ("live broadcast").

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá gǎndàole xiànchǎng.
examples.english: The police rushed to the scene.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì chǎng xiànchǎng biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: This is a live performance.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.

example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi shǐ wǒ hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: This news made me very happy.
example.fact: 使 is a causative verb in written Chinese, as in 使…高兴 ('make … happy'). It also means 'to use' in 使用 and 'envoy' in 大使 (ambassador). In casual speech 让 (ràng) is often used instead of 使.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息使大家很担心。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi shǐ dàjiā hěn dānxīn.
examples.english: This news made everyone worried.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī bǐ hěn hǎoshǐ.
examples.english: This pen is very easy to use.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.

example.pinyin: Qǐng xiàng zuǒ zhuǎn.
example.english: Please turn left.
example.fact: 转 has two readings: zhuǎn ('to turn, to transfer', as in 转弯 and 转学) and zhuàn ('to rotate, to wander', as in 转圈 and 转来转去). With 转 + noun it also means to forward things: 转发 (forward a message).

examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de lùkǒu xiàng yòu zhuǎn.
examples.english: Turn right at the intersection ahead.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ diànhuà zhuǎn gěi Wáng jīnglǐ.
examples.english: Please transfer the call to Manager Wang.

meanings: (old) person specialized in a skill or trade

example.hanzi: 她去年拿到了博士学位。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián nádào le bóshì xuéwèi.
example.english: She got her doctorate last year.
example.fact: 博士 literally reads as "broadly learned scholar" — 博 ("extensive, broad", tied here to 十 "ten" as a symbol of completeness) plus 士 ("scholar, gentleman") — and this literal sense was mapped directly onto the modern Western academic title "PhD" when Chinese needed a term for it in the early 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 博士,请您看一下这份报告。
examples.pinyin: Bóshì, qǐng nín kàn yíxià zhè fèn bàogào.
examples.english: Doctor, please take a look at this report.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài dú bóshì.
examples.english: He's working on his doctorate.

components.note: 十 (ten) — complete and wide: 博 is broad, abundant.
尃 (fū) is a loose sound clue for bó; 尃 also in 搏 bó, 薄 báo and 缚 fù.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.pinyin: Tā zhídào shēnyè cái huí jiā.
example.english: He didn't come home until late at night.
example.fact: 直到 commonly pairs with 才 in the pattern "直到 X, 才 Y" ("not until X did Y happen") — 才 carries the "only then" emphasis, so dropping it (直到深夜他回家了) sounds noticeably flatter to a native ear, one of several such fixed adverb pairings in Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 我们等了很久,直到他来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děngle hěn jiǔ, zhídào tā lái.
examples.english: We waited a long time, until he came.

examples.pinyin: Zhídào xiànzài, wǒ hái bù míngbai.
examples.english: Even now, I still don't understand.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.pinyin: Kǎoshì qián wǒ hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: I'm very nervous before the exam.
example.fact: 紧 (from 糸, thread pulled taut) and 张 (from 弓, a bow drawn taut) each independently picture something pulled tight — 紧张 stacks two 'taut' images into one word, making its abstract sense 'tense, nervous' a remarkably direct metaphor: feeling strung as tight as a drawn bowstring.

examples.pinyin: Tā yì jǐnzhāng jiù shuō bu chū huà.
examples.english: When he's nervous, he can't speak.

examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn gōngzuò hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Work has been intense lately.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).
弓 (bow) — bows and stretching, as in 弯 bend, 弹 pluck, 引 draw: 张 is to draw a bow.
长 (zhǎng) is a close sound clue for zhāng.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu èr gè háizi.
example.english: I have two children.
example.fact: 二 is used for counting and in numbers (二十, 第二), but before a measure word Chinese uses 两 instead: 两个人, not 二个人. Mixing them up is one of the most common mistakes for learners.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì èr yuè èr rì.
examples.english: Today is February 2nd.

examples.hanzi: 二月是一年里最短的月份。
examples.pinyin: Èr yuè shì yì nián lǐ zuì duǎn de yuèfèn.
examples.english: February is the shortest month of the year.

example.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé jiǎnzhí tài guì le!
example.english: This price is simply outrageous!
example.fact: Despite its parts literally meaning something closer to "simple" (简, from bamboo writing strips) and "straight" (直), 简直 functions as a pure intensifying adverb meaning "simply, just" before an exaggerated claim — much like English "simply" in "that's simply amazing" has drifted away from its literal sense of ease.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnzhí shì ge tiāncái.
examples.english: He's simply a genius.

examples.hanzi: 这里的风景简直像画一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng jiǎnzhí xiàng huà yíyàng.
examples.english: The scenery here is simply like a painting.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo strips, once written on, as in 笔, 等, 管: a slip, so simple and brief.
间 (jiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn.
目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.pinyin: Bié fàngqì nǐ de mèngxiǎng.
example.english: Don't give up on your dream.
example.fact: 放 ("to release, let go") plus 弃 (pictured as two hands 廾 casting aside a bundled object) combine almost literally into "to let go and throw away" — one of the more transparent compositional images in this batch, directly mirroring its modern sense "to give up, abandon."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì fàngqì xué Zhōngwén.
examples.english: I won't give up learning Chinese.

examples.pinyin: Tā fàngqìle zhè cì jīhuì.
examples.english: He gave up this opportunity.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
廾 (two hands) — hands throwing something out: 弃 is to cast away.

example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎozi pǎo de zhēn kuài.
example.english: That kid runs really fast.
example.fact: 小子 has two dictionary readings that are easy to conflate: the common, informal xiǎozi ("boy, lad, kid" — often a gruff or teasing address, as in 你这小子 "you little punk") that accounts for the word's real frequency, and a separate literary xiǎozǐ ("young man"; also an old, self-effacing "I/me" used when addressing an elder) — the same two characters, a different register entirely.

examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozi hěn cōngming.
examples.english: This kid is very smart.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè xiǎozi, yòu chídào le!
examples.english: You rascal, late again!

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 晚饭后我们一起看电视。
example.pinyin: Wǎnfàn hòu wǒmen yìqǐ kàn diànshì.
example.english: After dinner we watch TV together.
example.fact: 电视 is a purely modern coinage — 电 ("electricity", itself a lightning-bolt pictograph reused for the modern concept) plus 视 ("to view") — following the same 电+X pattern behind 电话 ("electric speech" = telephone) and 电脑 ("electric brain" = computer), Mandarin's default strategy for naming 20th-century technology.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài kètīng kàn diànshì.
examples.english: We're watching TV in the living room.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tái diànshì shì xīn mǎi de.
examples.english: This TV was newly bought.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.
弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.

example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ hěn qiáng.
example.english: His body is strong.
example.fact: 强 has the readings qiáng ('strong'), qiǎng ('to force', as in 勉强) and jiàng ('stubborn', as in 倔强). The strong reading shows up in 加强 (strengthen), 强大 (powerful), and 强调 (emphasise).

examples.pinyin: Tā de zérènxīn hěn qiáng.
examples.english: He has a strong sense of responsibility.

examples.hanzi: 这支球队比去年更强了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì bǐ qùnián gèng qiáng le.
examples.english: This team is stronger than last year.

example.hanzi: 不好意思,请问洗手间在哪儿?
example.pinyin: Bùhǎoyìsi, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 不好意思 works as a softer, more versatile cousin of 对不起: 对不起 apologizes for a real fault, while 不好意思 covers everything from mild embarrassment to a polite "(sorry to bother you,) excuse me" used to open a request to a stranger — a nuance its literal gloss, "not good meaning," doesn't capture at all.

examples.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ lái wǎn le.
examples.english: Sorry, I'm late.

examples.hanzi: 他被夸得有点不好意思。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi kuā de yǒudiǎn bù hǎoyìsi.
examples.english: He felt a bit embarrassed at being praised.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.

example.hanzi: 我们大概需要两个小时。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dàgài xūyào liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: We probably need about two hours.
example.fact: 概 originally named a wooden bar used to level off excess grain when measuring by the bushel — striking a rough, standard level rather than an exact one. That image of 'close enough, roughly leveled' carried over almost directly into 大概's modern sense, 'roughly, approximately.'

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài dàgài bā diǎn.
examples.english: It's about eight o'clock now.

examples.pinyin: Tā dàgài bú huì lái le.
examples.english: He probably won't come.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 概 first meant a wooden scraper that levelled grain.
既 (jì) is a close sound clue for gài; 既 also in 溉 gài and 慨 kǎi.

example.pinyin: Zhè díquè shì gè hǎo zhǔyi.
example.english: This really is a good idea.
example.fact: 的确 borrows the ubiquitous particle 的 (elsewhere just a possessive/adjective marker, as in 我的书 "my book") and fuses it with 确 ("true, certain") into a fixed adverb meaning "indeed, really" — a reminder that 的 shows up in several unrelated fixed words beyond its famous grammatical role.

examples.pinyin: Tā díquè hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: He really is hardworking.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de cài díquè búcuò.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is indeed good.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.
石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Zhège cài hěn tèbié.
example.english: This dish is very special.
example.fact: 特 means 'special' and 'especially': 特别 (special, very), 特点 (feature), 特色 (distinctive character) and 特地 (specially). It is also common in transliterations, as in 特朗普 (Trump).

examples.hanzi: 这家店的面条特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miàntiáo tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The noodles at this shop are especially tasty.

examples.hanzi: 我有一个特别的礼物给你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge tèbié de lǐwù gěi nǐ.
examples.english: I have a special gift for you.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yào ànshí chī yào.
example.english: You should take your medicine on time.
example.fact: 药 uses the verb 吃 in Chinese ('eat medicine'), and appears in 药店 (pharmacy), 药片 (tablet) and 药方 (prescription). It is also the root of 火药 (gunpowder), which is literally 'fire medicine'.

examples.pinyin: Gǎnmào le jiù yào chī yào.
examples.english: When you catch a cold, you need to take medicine.

examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn yàodiàn zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?

example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú huídào le jiā.
example.english: He finally returned home.
example.fact: 到 here works as a resultative verb complement meaning "the goal was reached" rather than a separate verb "to arrive" — attaching directly after 回 ("to return") to confirm the destination was reached, the same complement pattern that turns 收 ("to gather") into 收到 ("to receive") elsewhere in this batch.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shí diǎn cái huídào jiā.
examples.english: I only got home at ten.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng huídào zuòwèi shàng.
examples.english: Please return to your seat.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.pinyin: Nàge nánhái xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
example.english: That boy likes playing soccer.
example.fact: 男 pictures 力 ('strength') applied to 田 ('a field') — someone strong enough to farm, an agrarian image behind the character for 'male' — so 男孩 literally reads as 'strong-in-the-field child,' though today it's simply the everyday word for 'boy.'

examples.pinyin: Zhège nánhái jīnnián shí suì.
examples.english: This boy is ten years old.

examples.hanzi: 三个男孩在公园里玩球。
examples.pinyin: Sān ge nánhái zài gōngyuán lǐ wán qiú.
examples.english: Three boys are playing ball in the park.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan gǔdiǎn yīnyuè.
example.english: I really like classical music.
example.fact: 乐 is a genuine two-reading character: yuè for "music" (as here) and lè for "happy" (as in 快乐, "happy") — historically linked since music was seen as a source of joy, but a learner has to memorize which compound takes which reading, since guessing wrong (yīnlè instead of yīnyuè) is a common beginner slip.

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: He likes listening to music.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu yīnyuè hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: This piece of music sounds lovely.

components.note: 音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.pinyin: Nǐ shēntǐ hǎo ma?
example.english: How is your health?
example.fact: 身体 doubles as the everyday word for general health and physical condition beyond its literal sense "body" — asking 你身体好吗 ("is your body good?") is really asking "how is your health," a common greeting especially toward elders, not a question about physique.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shēntǐ bù shūfu.
examples.english: I don't feel well today.

examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Exercising more is good for your health.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.

example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu liúxuè le.
example.english: His hand is bleeding.
example.fact: 血 has two readings: xuè (in compounds and formal speech, as in 血液, 流血, 血型) and xiě (colloquially alone, as in 吐血 or 一口血). Both are heard, and the same character is also used in 热血 (passion).

examples.pinyin: Tā de bízi liúxuè le.
examples.english: His nose is bleeding.

examples.hanzi: 医生说我的血压有点高。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō wǒ de xuèyā yǒudiǎn gāo.
examples.english: The doctor said my blood pressure is a bit high.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi liúxià le.
example.english: He left the keys behind.
example.fact: 下 attached after a verb often marks something coming to rest or settling in place (坐下 'sit down', 停下 'stop') — 留下 uses that same complement to turn 留 ('to remain') into a precise 'leave behind, stay put', distinguishing it from 留 alone, which can also mean the more active 'to keep, retain' something.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ liúxià xìngmíng hé diànhuà.
examples.english: Please leave your name and phone number.

examples.hanzi: 你今天晚上可以留下吃饭吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān wǎnshang kěyǐ liúxià chīfàn ma?
examples.english: Can you stay for dinner tonight?

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的学习方式。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de xuéxí fāngshì.
example.english: Everyone has their own way of learning.
example.fact: 式 pictures a craftsman's tools — 弋 (an awl) and 工 (a measuring square) — used to make things to a fixed pattern, which is why so many "-式" words name a fixed style or method (方式 "way, method"; 正式 "formal"; 公式 "formula").

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fāngshì hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This method is very effective.

examples.pinyin: Tā de shuōhuà fāngshì hěn tèbié.
examples.english: His way of speaking is very distinctive.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu shòushāng le.
example.english: His hand was hurt.
example.fact: 伤 is a noun (伤口, wound) and a verb ('to hurt'), as in 伤心 (heartbroken) and 受伤 (to get injured). It also means 'to harm', as in 伤害.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié shāngdào shǒu.
examples.english: Be careful not to hurt your hand.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shang yǒu yí ge shāngkǒu.
examples.english: There's a wound on his leg.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn qíguài.
example.english: This matter is very strange.
example.fact: 怪 means 'strange' in 奇怪 and 怪不得 ('no wonder'), and 'to blame' in 别怪我 ('don't blame me'). Used as an adverb in 怪好看的 it means 'rather' (colloquial, northern).

examples.hanzi: 你别怪我，我真的忘记了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié guài wǒ, wǒ zhēn de wàngjì le.
examples.english: Don't blame me, I really forgot.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān yǒudiǎn qíguài.
examples.english: He is a bit strange today.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wàitào yào yìbǎi měiyuán.
example.english: This jacket costs a hundred dollars.
example.fact: 元 (from an image emphasizing a person's head — "first, foremost") became Mandarin's generic word for a basic currency unit, filled in by the country name: 美元 ("American" + 元) for the US dollar, 日元 for the Japanese yen, 欧元 for the Euro — the same slot, a different country each time.

examples.hanzi: 一美元等于多少人民币?
examples.pinyin: Yì měiyuán děngyú duōshao Rénmínbì?
examples.english: How many yuan is one US dollar?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā wǔshí měiyuán.
examples.english: I gave him fifty US dollars.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
元 (first, head) — a person with the head marked: 元 first meant the head, so first, chief, origin. 元 also gives 完 wán, 玩 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 他因为偷东西被送进了监狱。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi tōu dōngxi bèi sòngjìn le jiānyù.
example.english: He was sent to prison for stealing.
example.fact: 狱's own components stack two dog radicals (犭and 犬) around 讠("speech, dispute") — traditionally read as two dogs snarling on either side of an argument — a vivid ancient courtroom image behind the modern word for "prison, lawsuit."

examples.pinyin: Nà zuò jiānyù zài shān shàng.
examples.english: That prison is on the mountain.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiānyù lǐ zhùle wǔ nián.
examples.english: He spent five years in prison.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and language, as in 说, 语, 话; 读 is to read aloud.
卖 (mài) is only a loose hint for dú; it stands in for an older 賣, as in 牍 dú and 犊 dú.

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān dúshū.
example.english: He reads every day.
example.fact: 读 is to read aloud and to study: 读书 (read books, or go to school), 读音 (pronunciation) and 阅读 (reading). Note 读 is read dòu in the rare word 句读 (punctuation).

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì zěnme dú?
examples.english: How do you read this character?

examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué dú jīngjì.
examples.english: She studies economics at university.

example.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng zhèbiān zǒu.
example.english: Please come this way.
example.fact: 这边 pairs with 那边 ("that side") the same way 这个/那个 do — but where 这里 ("here") names a fixed point, 这边 leans toward a direction or side, which is why staff say 这边请 ("this way, please") rather than 这里请 when guiding someone somewhere.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zuò zhèbiān.
examples.english: Please sit over here.

examples.pinyin: Zhèbiān de fēngjǐng bǐ nàbiān hǎo.
examples.english: The view on this side is better than that side.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.pinyin: Qǐng chóngxīn tiánxiě zhè zhāng biǎogé.
example.english: Please fill out this form again, from scratch.
example.fact: 重新 implies starting completely over from scratch (重新开始 "start over"), while its near-synonym 再 just means "once more" without necessarily redoing everything (再说一次 "say it again") — a distinction easy to blur since English "again" covers both.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chóngxīn kāishǐ.
examples.english: I want to start over.

examples.hanzi: 电脑坏了,我得重新安装。
examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo huài le, wǒ děi chóngxīn ānzhuāng.
examples.english: The computer broke; I have to reinstall it.

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
目 (eye) — 目 marks the eye and looking, as in 看, 眼, 睛; 瞧 is to look.
焦 (jiāo) — near sound — 瞧 is qiáo; 焦 also sounds out 憔 qiáo.

example.pinyin: Nǐ qiáo, tā lái le.
example.english: Look, he's here.
example.fact: 瞧 is a colloquial word for 'look', used mostly in northern speech: 瞧一瞧 (have a look) and 瞧不起 (look down on). It's less formal than 看.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ qiáo, nà zhī xiǎoniǎo duō kě'ài!
examples.english: Look, how cute that little bird is!

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ qiáoqiao nǐ de xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: Let me have a look at your new phone.

example.hanzi: 演唱会现场的粉丝们疯狂地欢呼。
example.pinyin: Yǎnchànghuì xiànchǎng de fěnsīmen fēngkuáng de huānhū.
example.english: The fans at the concert cheered wildly.
example.fact: 狂 traces back to a rabid, mad dog (犭), while 疯 pairs the "sickness" radical 疒 with the phonetic 风 ("wind") — pairing an illness-word for madness with an animal-word for wildness, 疯狂 doubles up two independently vivid pictures of losing control.

examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ tài fēngkuáng le!
examples.english: This idea is too crazy!

examples.pinyin: Tā fēngkuáng de àishàngle yīnyuè.
examples.english: He fell madly in love with music.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — illness, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain, 疼 ache: madness is an illness.
风 (fēng, wind) gives the exact sound; also in 枫 fēng.
犭 (dog, animal) — animals, as in 狗, 猫, 猪: a wild animal.
王 (wáng) is a loose sound clue for kuáng; 王 also in 往 wǎng and 旺 wàng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān shōudào le nǐ de xìn.
example.english: I received your letter yesterday.
example.fact: 收 alone just means 'to gather, collect' without guaranteeing success — attaching the complement 到 ('arriving, reaching') turns it into 收到, confirming that whatever was sent actually arrived, the same success-marking job 到 does after 看 (看到, 'to see') and 听 (听到, 'to hear').

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shōudào wǒ de yóujiàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you receive my email?

examples.hanzi: 她收到了一份生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shōudàole yí fèn shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: She received a birthday present.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我们讨论了几个方案,其中一个很有创意。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen tǎolùn le jǐ gè fāng'àn, qízhōng yí gè hěn yǒu chuàngyì.
example.english: We discussed a few proposals, one of which was very creative.
example.fact: 其中 always points back to a group already named in the sentence or context — it can't introduce a brand-new set the way English "among" sometimes can, which is why it almost always follows a list or plural noun ("几个方案,其中...") rather than opening a sentence on its own.

examples.hanzi: 这些书其中有一本是我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū qízhōng yǒu yì běn shì wǒ de.
examples.english: One of these books is mine.

examples.hanzi: 他有三个孩子,其中两个已经工作了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu sān ge háizi, qízhōng liǎng ge yǐjīng gōngzuò le.
examples.english: He has three children, two of whom already work.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí piàn miànbāo.
example.english: Please give me a slice of bread.
example.fact: 片 is a measure word for flat things (一片叶子, 一片面包) and a noun for film or cards: 电影片, 照片 (photo), 名片 (business card). In 片 as 'film' it can also read piān in 片儿 (a flat piece, spoken).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí piàn miànbāo.
examples.english: I'd like to eat a slice of bread.

examples.hanzi: 我们昨天去看了一部好片子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuótiān qù kànle yí bù hǎo piànzi.
examples.english: We went to see a good film yesterday.

example.hanzi: 我对这个问题有不同的想法。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhège wèntí yǒu bùtóng de xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: I have a different idea about this issue.
example.fact: 法 pictures water (氵) following a fixed course (去) — a natural, regulated way of flowing that gave the character its sense "method, way" — 想法 literally combines this with 想 ("to think") into "a way of thinking," Mandarin's everyday word for a personal idea or opinion.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme xiǎngfǎ?
examples.english: What's your idea?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu zhè zhǒng xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: I don't have that kind of thought.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 我下个月要去纽约旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiàgèyuè yào qù Niǔyuē lǚxíng.
example.english: I'm traveling to New York next month.
example.fact: 纽约 is a pure sound-transliteration of "New York" — 纽 ("knot, button") and 约 ("approximately, to agree") were picked only for how close niǔ-yuē sounds to the English name, with no attempt to translate the actual meaning of "new" or "york," unlike semantic coinages such as 电视 ("electric-view" for television) elsewhere in this batch.

examples.pinyin: Niǔyuē de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
examples.english: Winters in New York are very cold.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài Niǔyuē gōngzuòle sān nián.
examples.english: He worked in New York for three years.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 结: a knot or button.
丑 (chǒu) is a loose sound clue for niǔ; 丑 also in 扭 niǔ and 钮 niǔ.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.

example.pinyin: Māma zài jiālǐ zuòfàn.
example.english: Mom is cooking at home.
example.fact: 家 alone can mean "home" as an abstract concept or "family," but 家里 anchors it with 里 ("inside") to mean specifically "inside the house, at home" as a physical location — the difference shows up in phrases like 回家 ("go home," a destination) versus 在家里 ("be at home," a location).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài bú zài jiālǐ.
examples.english: I'm not at home now.

examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ yǒu kèrén.
examples.english: There are guests at home.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.
灬 (fire dots) — fire and heat: 热, 点, 煮, 照; 黑 is soot and smoke from a flame.

example.pinyin: Tiān yǐjīng hēi le.
example.english: It is already dark.
example.fact: 黑 means 'black' and 'dark', as in 黑夜 (night), 黑板 (blackboard), and slang like 黑客 (hacker) and 黑名单 (blacklist). It can also be used of 'illegal': 黑车 (unlicensed car).

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang wàimiàn hěn hēi.
examples.english: It's very dark outside at night.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa shì hēisè de.
examples.english: His hair is black.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshang méi dài qián.
example.english: I'm not carrying any money.
example.fact: 身 is body, as in 身体, 身高 (height) and 身份 (identity), and also a measure word for suits of clothes: 一身衣服. In 身上 it means 'on one's person'.

examples.pinyin: Tā shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He is in good health.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshang de yīfu shī le.
examples.english: The clothes on me are wet.

example.pinyin: Wǒ háiyào yì bēi kāfēi, xièxie.
example.english: I'd like one more cup of coffee, thanks.
example.fact: 还要 stacks two separate senses of 还 — "still" (as in 还没, "not yet") and "in addition, also" — onto 要 ("to want, need, will"), so depending on context it can mean "I still want (more)" (我还要一个) or "I also need to (do something)" (我还要去银行), two related but distinct translations packed into the same two characters.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ hái yào diǎn biéde ma?
examples.english: Do you want to order anything else?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái yào yì wǎn mǐfàn.
examples.english: I also want a bowl of rice.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: 还 is to go back or return (huán), then "still" (hái).
不 here stands in for 睘 (huán) in the traditional 還, so it is not a real clue; same stand-in in 环 huán.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.pinyin: Tā zài zuòyè shang xiě míngzi.
example.english: He writes his name on the homework.
example.fact: 作 is a verb meaning 'to make, do', in 工作 (work), 作业 (homework), 作用 (effect), 作者 (author) and 作为 (as). It is mostly used in formal compounds, whereas 做 is the casual form for 'to do'.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang zuò zuòyè.
examples.english: He does his homework every evening.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works at a company.

example.pinyin: Yínháng jiù zài chāoshì hòumian.
example.english: The bank is right behind the supermarket.
example.fact: 面 (originally a pictograph of a face) works as a locative suffix turning a direction into a place-noun — 后面 ("behind") mirrors 前面 ("in front"), 上面 ("above"), and 里面 ("inside"), all built from the same "-面" pattern for naming relative position.

examples.pinyin: Tā duǒ zài mén hòumian.
examples.english: He hid behind the door.

examples.pinyin: Hòumian de tóngxué tīng bu dào.
examples.english: The students in the back can't hear.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.pinyin: Zhège háizi xìnggé hěn hǎo.
example.english: This child has a good character.
example.fact: 性 is a suffix that turns words into abstract nouns, like 可能性 (possibility) and 重要性 (importance), and it also means 'gender' (性别) or 'nature' (个性).

examples.pinyin: Tā de xìnggé hěn kāilǎng.
examples.english: She has a very cheerful personality.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏适合女性玩家。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì shìhé nǚxìng wánjiā.
examples.english: This game suits female players.

example.hanzi: 这个消息给大家带来了希望。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi gěi dàjiā dàilái le xīwàng.
example.english: This news brought hope to everyone.
example.fact: 带 ("to carry along") plus the directional complement 来 ("toward the speaker") literally means "carry here" — but 带来 is used just as often in its figurative sense, "to bring about (a result, an effect)," as in 带来影响 ("to bring about an impact"), extending the physical carrying image to abstract causes and consequences.

examples.hanzi: 好天气给我们带来好心情。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo tiānqì gěi wǒmen dàilái hǎo xīnqíng.
examples.english: Nice weather brings us a good mood.

examples.pinyin: Bié wàngle dàilái nǐ de shū.
examples.english: Don't forget to bring your book.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
